Quite for YouTube

YouTube, without the advertising.

Free MIT ChromeEdgeBraveArc

Add to Chrome, it's free View the source ›

1 permission · Runs only on YouTube · No tracking · MIT licensed

Quite for YouTube deals with advertising in two places at once. Video ads are got past: Skip is clicked the moment it appears, and unskippable ads are fast-forwarded. The ad panels scattered through the homepage, sidebar, search results and masthead never paint at all, because they are hidden before the page renders.

The interesting part is what it does not do. YouTube's responses are never modified. Instead the ad schedule is stopped at source: the request the player sends is declared as an ad unit rather than a watch page, and YouTube answers without an ad schedule of its own. Nothing is deleted and nothing is faked, so there is no mismatch between what the server sent and what the player sees. That mismatch is exactly what YouTube's anti-adblock check looks for.

What it does

6 things, and no more.

Video ads, got past

Skip is clicked as soon as it appears and unskippable ads are fast-forwarded. Seeking is a last resort that never touches anything longer than three minutes, because that is not an ad.

Feed ads never paint

Homepage, sidebar, search results and the masthead banner are hidden before the page renders, so there is no flicker of an ad you then watch disappear.

Player overlays gone

The banners drawn on top of the video while you are watching it are removed along with everything else.

Merch shelves, if you want

Product shelves under videos can go too. Off by default, because some people actually use them.

Stopped at source, not faked

The ad schedule is never edited after the fact. That is what keeps the session out of YouTube's anti-adblock net, and why videos still play normally.

Diagnostics built in

The popup shows the version actually running in the page and reports what it has done this session, with a Copy report button for when something needs looking at.

Installing it

One click from the Chrome Web Store. The unpacked route below still works if you would rather run the source.

Add to Chrome

  1. 1

    Download the latest release and unzip it. You need the folder. Keep it somewhere permanent, because moving or deleting it stops the extension working.

  2. 2

    Open chrome://extensions in your browser.

  3. 3

    Turn on Developer mode, top right.

  4. 4

    Click Load unpacked and select the folder you unzipped.

  5. 5

    Reload any YouTube tab you already had open.

Chrome shows a "Developer mode extensions" warning each time it starts. That is normal for anything installed outside the Web Store, and it can be dismissed.

Latest news

Releases and breakages for Quite for YouTube.

29 August 2026 Breakage Quite for YouTube

Some videos start black and silent instead of playing

On some videos an advert still gets through. When it does, the player can sit black and silent instead of playing either the advert or your video. It looks like the extension has broken, which is the worst way for this to fail, so it is worth saying plainly what is happening.

The extension does not block requests. It stops YouTube issuing an ad schedule in the first place, which is what keeps your session out of the anti-adblock net. It does not catch every response, and on the ones it misses an advert starts inside a player that was not expecting one.

There is deliberately no automatic recovery. An earlier version reloaded the player after a stall; measured over repeated loads it produced a YouTube error screen more often than it rescued anything, so it was taken out. A stuck video you can reload is better than an error screen you cannot.

Reload the video and it usually plays. If it sticks again, add ?ytacoff=1 to the end of the URL. That loads that one video with the extension switched off, which is also how to confirm the extension is what is causing it rather than YouTube having a bad day.

This is why the store listing says most video ads rather than all of them. Claiming otherwise would earn one-star reviews describing exactly this.

What still works

  • Feed, sidebar, search and Shorts ad panels are still hidden
  • Overlay banners drawn on top of the video are still removed
  • Most video ads are still stopped before they load, and skippable ones still get skipped
  • Nothing about your account, watch history or any other tab is touched

What it asks for

1 permission and one site, and why each is there.

storage
To remember your checkbox settings. That is the only thing it stores, and it stores it in your own browser.
*://*.youtube.com/*
The extension runs on YouTube and nowhere else. It has no permission to read, or even see, any other site you visit.

Chrome shows you this list at install time. We would rather you saw it first. The source is public, so you can check that it is the whole list.

Questions

Why not just use a normal ad blocker?

Network-level blockers trigger YouTube's anti-adblock wall. This works differently. It stops the ad schedule being issued rather than blocking the request afterwards. Running both at once is worse than running either, because you cannot tell which caused what.

Will I still see an ad start?

Briefly, sometimes. The default is to let the ad begin and then get past it. On one verified session of 37 live ads: 35 skipped, 2 fast-forwarded, 2 seeked, and no false seeks.

It stopped working after a YouTube update.

YouTube changes its player regularly, and skipping can break until the extension catches up. Expected rather than a regression. Click the icon to check the version actually running in the page, and reload the extension if it does not match what you installed.

Does it work on Edge or Brave?

Yes. It runs in Chrome, Edge, Brave, Arc, Opera and other Chromium browsers.
